title: Usage Insights: export job creation + download flow (CSV/JSON) w/ limits + audit events
creator: Logan Wright
project: In-console usage insights (cost drivers by route)
description:
Goal
Implement the export job workflow for Usage Insights so customers can generate a bounded report (CSV + JSON) from console filters and download it later. Must enforce limits to prevent timeouts and cost blowups, and must generate compliance-grade audit logs for create/download.

Context
Usage Insights introduces route/model dimensions and top-cost-driver views. Finance/ops workflows need a report export to attach to cost reviews and internal incident docs. Several design partners explicitly asked for route-level spend exports with model breakdown.

Scope
1) Export Job API + lifecycle
- Create export: accepts same filter model as the dashboards (time window, org/project, deployment mode, region, environment, route filter/search, model filter, breakdown options).
- Async generation (no synchronous “stream the whole query” from the create call).
- Job states: queued -> running -> succeeded | failed | expired | canceled.
- Poll job status endpoint.
- Download endpoint once succeeded.

2) Output formats
- CSV: human/finance friendly. Stable headers + documented schema.
- JSON: machine-friendly, mirrors API response structure used by the console (but still bounded and versioned).

3) Guardrails (hard requirements)
- Time range bounding and row limits.
- File size cap.
- Query cost budget/timeouts.
- Per-org rate limiting on export creation.
- Retention/expiry for generated artifacts.

4) RBAC + tenant isolation
- Exports MUST respect org/project scoping identical to insights APIs.
- The download path must re-check authorization (not only at create time).

5) Audit logging
- Emit audit events on export creation and on download attempts (success/failure).
- Include actor + filters + artifact metadata necessary for compliance evidence.

Non-goals
- Scheduled exports.
- Customer-defined custom dimensions.
- Multi-month historical exports beyond retention.

Proposed API (draft)
- POST /v1/usage-insights/exports
  - body: { time_start, time_end, granularity, filters..., format: csv|json, include: [route_summary, model_breakdown], sort, limit }
  - response: { export_id, status, created_at, expires_at }
- GET /v1/usage-insights/exports/{export_id}
  - response: { export_id, status, progress?, created_at, started_at, finished_at, expires_at, result: { format, rows, bytes } }
- GET /v1/usage-insights/exports/{export_id}/download
  - response: file download (stream) OR 302 to signed URL (short TTL)

Decisions to finalize in this ticket
A) Limits (initial GA defaults)
- Max time range per export: 31 days (hourly rollup) OR 90 days (daily rollup). If request exceeds, return 400 with guidance.
- Max rows: 200,000 rows for CSV; 50,000 objects for JSON.
- Max bytes: 50 MB per artifact.
- Max concurrent running exports per org: 3.
- Export create rate limit: 10/hour per org (burst 3).
- Retention: artifact expires after 7 days.

B) File schema stability
- CSV must include schema_version column and a stable header set.
- JSON must include top-level schema_version field (string) and a “generated_at” timestamp.
- Backward-compatible changes only without version bump (append-only columns, optional fields).

C) Storage + security
- Store artifacts in internal blob storage bucket with SSE + per-env isolation.
- If using signed URLs, TTL 10 minutes. Download endpoint should require auth and re-check RBAC before issuing a signed URL.
- All export artifacts should be tagged with org_id + project_id for operational sweeps and cleanup.

Implementation plan
1) Data selection
- Use aggregates from ENG-8422 (hourly/daily route/model cost tables). Avoid raw event scans.
- Ensure the export uses the same canonical route/model normalization behavior as the UI APIs.

2) Job runner
- Background job that materializes results into CSV/JSON and uploads artifact.
- Ensure idempotency: repeated worker execution should not create multiple artifacts (same export_id).
- Handle late-arriving data: export reflects the aggregates as-of job start time; include a “data_freshness_lag_seconds” field where available.

3) Failure modes
- If query exceeds budget or times out -> job failed with code EXPORT_QUERY_TIMEOUT.
- If artifact too large -> job failed with code EXPORT_SIZE_LIMIT.
- If filters invalid or unauthorized -> return 400/403 at create time; still audit the attempt.

Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Create export succeeds for bounded filters and returns export_id.
- [ ] Job progresses to succeeded and produces downloadable artifact.
- [ ] CSV + JSON exports match the corresponding API results for the same filter window (within documented reconciliation tolerances).
- [ ] Limits enforced with clear error messages (400) and docs-friendly guidance.
- [ ] Download endpoint re-checks RBAC; cross-project leakage test passes.
- [ ] Audit events emitted:
  - usage_insights.export.created
  - usage_insights.export.downloaded (or attempted + outcome)
  - usage_insights.export.failed (optional but preferred)
- [ ] Metrics emitted: job queue lag, job duration p50/p95, success rate, failure reason counts, artifact bytes, download count.
- [ ] Load test: 31-day hourly export of top routes completes < 60s p95 in staging with 20 concurrent jobs across orgs (subject to the concurrency limit).

Notes / open questions
- Should we support “signed URL only” downloads, or always stream from Redwood API? Prefer signed URL for large files, but must preserve audit logging (audit at issuance + on download attempt).
- JSON shape: do we export a flat row list (CSV-like) or nested (route -> models)? If nested, keep it bounded and document schema_version evolution.
- Do we include cached token fields and GPU time proxy now, or keep v1 minimal? PM preference is include cached tokens to unblock FinOps questions.

comments: 2026-02-07 (Paula Mendes): Please prioritize hard limits + actionable error copy. We’ve already seen prospects try to export “last 6 months”. If we can’t support it, we need explicit messaging + a doc link in the error response.

2026-02-08 (Kevin Osei): Audit logging needs to capture the exact filters, format, and the resolved scope (org_id/project_id). Also make sure download is audited even if the signed URL is used. Recommendation: audit on /download issuance + include url_ttl_seconds; optionally add a lightweight redirect service that logs the actual GET on the signed URL path if feasible.

2026-02-10 (Allison Grant): Please emit job duration + bytes metrics with high-cardinality labels avoided (no route/model labels). Also add an alert candidate for export failure rate > 5% over 30m and for p95 job duration > 120s.

2026-02-12 (Jada Williams): Drafted job table schema: export_id, org_id, project_id, actor_id, status, format, filters_json, created_at, updated_at, expires_at, artifact_uri, artifact_bytes, row_count, failure_code. Will keep filters_json as canonical request body for audit + debugging, but will redact any free-form search strings if they can contain user data (TBD; likely OK but will confirm).

2026-02-14 (Nadia Rahman): Strong preference to export from aggregates only. If a filter combination would require scanning raw metering events, we should reject with 400 (unsupported) rather than silently running a slow query.

2026-02-18 (Kaitlyn Nguyen): RBAC: ensure export creation checks project membership AND download path re-checks membership. Also ensure exports created in project A cannot be downloaded by a token scoped only to project B even within same org.

2026-02-21 (Logan Wright): Aligning on limits: 31 days hourly / 90 days daily; 200k CSV row cap; 50MB size cap; retention 7 days. Next step is wiring download to signed URL with 10m TTL and ensuring audit events include outcome=issued + outcome=denied for unauthorized downloads.
